units: frozen at run time by `ousast learn experiment units` from the memory after the negatives harvest (merged in 5b2bd9b, 1133 static examples), committed, and registered again before the run; until then the run refuses (check_registered: the units file does not exist)
requirement: learned-decision-engine Req 6.4, amended 2026-10-03 by maintainer decision (refines the BLOCK rule of Req 7.3 and 7.4)
kind: rule: one zero-cost scoring pass of the six slice-2 incumbent programs; arms differ only in the BLOCK rule
zero_cost: the run replays the response cache behind a zero-ceiling meter; a unit with any uncached response is excluded and counted. The harvest changed the memory the programs retrieve from, so a paid cache fill, approved separately with its own ceiling, must precede the run

normalisation.choice: per-family Platt scaling: learn.calibrate.fit_map with its existing floors (own slope and intercept per family at >= 20 positive and negative repository groups, a pooled slope with a per-family intercept at >= 10, no map below that and so no BLOCK for that family on that fold), fitted on the training folds' paired units only
normalisation.why: a rank-to-quantile map gives every family the same flag rate whatever its precision, so one pooled threshold would flag the top slice of a weak family as readily as of a strong one; Platt puts each family on the scale of its own training precision, which a pooled precision bound needs. The map is a normaliser only: precision is shown by the held-out bound, not by calibration (exp-003: ECE <= 0.05 does not hold per family)

arms.A: today's rule: Platt map cross-fitted per family; BLOCK only when the calibration check holds; BLOCK point nested on the other folds' calibrated p (Wilson LB >= 0.95)
arms.B: pooled gate: per outer fold j, training units normalised by an inner cross-fit; t_block = the lowest normalised score whose Wilson 95% LB of precision over the training paired flags of all families together is >= 0.95 (unsure never flags); t_quiet per family = the highest normalised score keeping >= 90% of that family's training paired positives; fold j's units BLOCK at p >= t_block, ADVISORY at p >= t_quiet (or without a map or t_quiet), silent below

family_floor.rule: a family may block only if its own held-out paired flags (all five folds) number >= 10 with zero errors; otherwise its flags are reported as ADVISORY. The floor uses held-out labels to decide which families block and moves no threshold
family_floor.why: zero errors in 10 flags is unlikely for a family much worse than the bar (probability 0.056 at precision 0.75, 0.107 at 0.80); a larger F is out of reach of the smaller families (16-19 paired positives in exp-003's units over all folds); 10 is exp-003 arm C's training minimum

primary_metric: held-out (outer-fold) Wilson 95% lower bound of flagged precision over arm B's paired flags of all families together, before the family floor (so dropping a failing family cannot raise it)

populations.primary: paired (both sides of the candidate present)

secondary_metrics: per-family flagged precision and Wilson LB
quiet_recall per family (held-out positives at or above t_quiet / positives) against 0.90
repository-cluster bootstrap 95% CI of flagged precision
decision_rule: on arm B's held-out paired flags of all families together, before the floor: REJECT B if their point precision < 0.95; else ADOPT B if their Wilson 95% LB >= 0.95 and at least one family passes the floor (>= 10 held-out paired flags, zero errors) -- those families block, every other family stays advisory; else INCONCLUSIVE (the incumbent rule stays)
power: the pooled bound needs >= 73 flags with no error (110 with one, 142 with two). On exp-003's units (all 353 scored, result-complete-cache.json) few paired positives rank above the first negative per family on the raw score (access control 10, deserialization 7, injection 2, output encoding 0, path 8, untrusted destination 5); normalisation keeps each family's order, so the pooled top set reaches 73 only if the harvest's pairs separate better. An inconclusive verdict is a plausible outcome
